MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 13, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 6:00 p.m. and the City Council convened into closed session in the City
Hall Conference Room, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Director of Community Development & Public Works David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton

CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Los Angeles Superior Court Case No. 19TRCV00130; Dr. Hendrik Baars, D.D.S. v.
  SRE DCM PV, LLC; City of Rolling Hills Estates

  AUTHORIZED THE CITY ATTORNEY’S OFFICE TO ISSUE A NOTICE OF
  VIOLATION TO DR. HENDRIK BAARS REGARDING HIS UNLAWFUL USE AND
  OPERATION OF A DENTAL OFFICE AT 27520 HAWTHORNE BLVD. BASED ON
  THE CITY’S MUNICIPAL CODE AND ENTITLEMENTS ISSUED BY THE CITY TO
  THE PROPERTY OWNER, SRE DCM PV, LLC., IN 2016.

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR
  Government Code Section 54957.6
  City representative: City Council
  Unrepresented employees: City Manager, Assistant City Manager, Administrative
  Services Director, Community Development/Public Works Director

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

  ***

MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the Closed Session portion of the meeting at 6:50 p.m. and the City
Council took a brief recess.

At 7:01 p.m., MAYOR MITCHELL called the meeting back to order in open session in the City
Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
AUGUST 13, 2019
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Paul Jensen and Joel Yamada, members of Boy Scout Troop 378, led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Director of Community Development & Public Works David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Michael Whitehead
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

Others Present:  Captain James Powers, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Dept., Lomita Station
  Farhad Iranitalab, City Traffic Engineer (Willdan)
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy (Willdan)

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown
  by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ and COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that they
  would abstain from voting on Items 5B and 5C because they were not present at those
  meetings.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A AND D-H
  AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
AUGUST 13, 2019
 B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 25, 2019

  APPROVED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED MINUTES OF JULY 8, 2019

  APPROVED.

D.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JULY 23, 2019

  APPROVED.

  APPROVED WARRANTS 61724 THROUGH 61826 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $120,162.31; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 070519 THROUGH 070619;
  080119 THROUGH 080319 IN THE AMOUNT OF $180,393.61 FOR A GRAND

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Captain James Powers, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department addressed the City Council to
introduce himself to the community as the Lomita Station’s new Captain. Captain Powers shared
his background and some of his philosophies for effective law enforcement. He commented that
the community’s quality of life is his concern and he is an advocate for partnerships in the
community. He invited the community to the “Coffee with a Cop” event at the Sheriff’s Department’s
substation at the Promenade on the Peninsula on Saturday, August 17 from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00
a.m.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
AUGUST 13, 2019
 PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

NONE.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  DRAFT COMMENT LETTER TO THE CITY OF TORRANCE ON THE DRAFT
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT (DEIR) PREPARED FOR THE SOLANA
  RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED IN THE CITY OF TORRANCE AT
  THE SOUTHWEST CORNER OF HAWTHORNE BLVD. AND VIA VALMONTE.

  Recommendation: That the City Council review and direct staff to send the attached draft
  letter to the City of Torrance, which provides the City of Rolling Hills Estates’ comments
  on the Draft Environmental Impact Report on the proposed 248-unit Solana Residential
  Project, located in the City of Torrance at the southwest corner of Hawthorne Blvd. and
  Via Val Monte.

  Director of Community Development & Public Works Wahba provided a staff report (as
  per the agenda material). He noted that two additional correspondence were received
  from Alexis Nielsen (Sugarhill Drive) and the Rollingwood Home Owners Association; and
  those correspondence were forwarded to the City Council via e-mail and placed on the
  dais.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF regarding the letter’s mention of the potential
  that toxic chemicals may have been dumped at the site, Director Wahba stated that based
  on information currently available, staff is asking that the matter be studied further.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ commented that she appreciates staff’s thoroughness and
  attention to detail, specifically with respect to the comment regarding the faulty traffic
  impact study and potential air quality impacts.

  MAYOR MITCHELL commented that she too is concerned about the traffic impact
  analysis specifically, the use of 2016 data and the Assumed Growth Factor that was used
  in the calculations.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki commented that she and Farhad Iranitalab, the City’s
  Traffic Engineer, reviewed the traffic impact study and it seems to have a number of errors
  including incorrect data for the turning volumes, which will affect air quality impacts.

  In response to MAYOR MITCHELL’S concern regarding the Assumed Growth Factor
  (AGF) used, Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki commented that is her understanding that
  they used an AGF of one percent, but it has been requested that they provide background
  and support for the decision to use that factor. She also noted concern regarding the fact
  that 2016 data is being used.

  Recognizing that there were members of the public present regarding this item, MAYOR
  MITCHELL asked for comments.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
AUGUST 13, 2019
   Donna Tarr, 63 Ranchview Road expressed concern regarding the traffic impacts,
  specifically the need to safely leave the area in the event of a wildfire a fire; and the
  potential toxic substances in the soil. She shared a flyer containing information on an
  upcoming meeting of the “Save Our Neighborhoods, Torrance” group.

  Judy Bain, Ponderosa Lane also expressed concern regarding the general traffic impacts.
  She further suggested the need to address the issues regarding safety and fire
  evacuation.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that the Human Health Risk Assessment was
  done under the old standard and it may be better to do the calculation using the new
  standard.

  MAYOR MITCHELL commented that this project is in the very beginning stages and that
  City Council and staff will continue to monitor the project as it moves through the process.

  Ms. Tarr noted for the public’s information that any individual can submit a comment letter
  on this project.

  Following discussion and public comment, the CITY COUNCIL concurred on the following
  direction:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO SEND THE LETTER PROVIDING THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES’ COMMENTS ON THE DEIR FOR THE PROPOSED
  248-UNIT SOLANA RESIDENTIAL PROJECT TO THE CITY OF TORRANCE TO
  INCLUDE EMPHASIS ON THE OUTDATED OFFICE OF ENVIRONMENTAL
  HEALTH HAZARD ASSESSMENT (OEHHA) ANALYSIS OF THE HEALTH
  RISKS AND POINT OUT THE DANGERS OF THE TRAFFIC IMPACTS SHOULD
  THERE BE A NEED TO EVACUATE IN THE EVENT OF AN EMERGENCY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

Recognizing that there were members of the public present regarding Item 8C, MAYOR
MITCHELL suggested taking that item out of order. Hearing no objection, she so ordered.

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE
  REQUEST

  Recommendation: That the City Council deny the request from Silver Spur Little League
  for placement of a score keepers’ shed at Ernie Howlett Park ball field.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF regarding the proposed location for the
  drinking fountain, Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated that the location
  proposed is near a water source, but there is some flexibility in where to install the drinking
  fountain.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
AUGUST 13, 2019
   Mike Shull, RPV Resident and Silver Spur Little League Board Member expressed his
  appreciation for the longstanding partnership SSLL has had with the City. He stated that
  the shed has been removed and if the League decides to pursue any such structure or
  project in the future, it will follow the proper process and procedures. Regarding the
  drinking fountain, he suggested that it not be installed directly behind home plate.

  Peter Cho, Silver Spur Little League President stated that the League may be interested
  in installing a scorekeepers’ shed/announcers shed in the future but will follow the proper
  procedures.

  Adam Brown, Silver Spur Little League Board Member expressed the importance of
  having a scorekeepers’ shed available for the participants in the league.

  Following discussion and public comment, the CITY COUNCIL concurred on the following
  direction:

  DIRECTED SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE OFFICIALS TO WORK WITH
  STAFF AND THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION IN ASSESSING THE
  NEEDS OF THE ORGANIZATION AND DETERMINING IF THERE MAY BE AN
  OPPORTUNITY TO LOCATE A SCOREKEEPERS’ SHED/ANNOUNCERS’
  SHED AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK IN THE FUTURE.

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: PROPOSED WALL OF
  RECOGNITION PLAQUES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the addition of bronze plaques on the
  Wall of Recognition honoring Douglas Prichard and Andrew Clark’s tenures with the City.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the unveiling of the plaques,
  City Manager Grammer stated that it would be staff’s recommendation that the plaques
  be unveiled in two separate ceremonies. The CITY COUNCIL concurred.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE ADDITION OF BRONZE PLAQUES
  ON THE WALL OF RECOGNITION HONORING DOUGLAS PRICHARD AND
  ANDREW CLARK’S TENURES WITH THE CITY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
AUGUST 13, 2019
 D.  REQUEST FOR SUPPORT OF PROPOSED LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES 2019
  ANNUAL CONFERENCE RESOLUTION ON RULE 20A PROJECTS FUNDING

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to submit a letter in support
  of the City of Rancho Palos Verdes’ effort to bring a resolution for consideration at the
  League of California Cities Annual 2019 Conference to amend Rule 20A to add projects
  in Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones to the list of eligibility criteria and to increase
  funding allocations for Rule 20A projects.

  City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SUBMIT A LETTER
  IN SUPPORT OF THE CITY OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES’ EFFORT TO BRING
  A RESOLUTION FOR CONSIDERATION AT THE LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA
  CITIES 2019 ANNUAL CONFERENCE TO AMEND RULE 20A TO ADD
  PROJECTS IN VERY HIGH FIRE HAZARD SEVERITY ZONES TO THE LIST OF
  ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA AND TO INCREASE FUNDING ALLOCATIONS FOR
  RULE 20A PROJECTS.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

OLD BUSINESS

A.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING FOR USE OF PALOS VERDES PENINSULA
  HIGH SCHOOL SWIMMING POOL AND REVISED RENTAL FEES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached revised Memorandum of
  Understanding between the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District and the City
  of Rolling Hills Estates and the City of Rancho Palos Verdes for Use of Pool Facilities at
  Palos Verdes Peninsula High School beginning June 1, 2019 and ending May 30, 2024.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  City Attorney Davis noted one administrative change that the City or Rancho Palos
  Verdes should be added to the title block of the MOU.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE REVISED MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA UNIFIED
  SCHOOL DISTRICT, THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AND THE CITY
  OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES FOR USE OF POOL FACILITIES AT PALOS
  VERDES PENINSULA HIGH SCHOOL BEGINNING JUNE 1, 2019 AND ENDING
  ON MAY 20, 2024.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
AUGUST 13, 2019
 B.  REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the scope of services and cost of Option
  B for a chemical-free Landscape Maintenance Services Agreement with Bennett
  Landscape, subject to approval as to from by the City Attorney, in the amount of $297,293
  in year one; $289,043 in year two; $274,590 in year three; $260,860 in year four; AND
  $246,796 in year five and adjust the Fiscal Year 2019-20 budget accordingly.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  Sean Bennett, Bennett Landscape addressed the City Council to further explain the scope
  of service and the benefits of the current proposal for a chemical-free landscape
  maintenance services agreement.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN, Mr. Bennett stated that with the
  program as proposed he doesn’t see a need to use pre-emergent herbicide.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that the City will be paying approximately
  $180,000 over five years to achieve a pesticide free landscape maintenance program and
  asked if the City would see a reduction in the cost after the five year period once the
  mulch has been distributed.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’S inquiry, Mr. Bennett stated that the
  mulch material will eventually biodegrade and will have to be replenished over the years
  so there likely will be no additional cost savings after the initial five year term.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ expressed her appreciation to Bennett Landscape and staff
  for their diligent efforts in developing a feasible solution.

  MAYOR MITCHELL noted concern regarding a statement in Mr. Bennett’s proposal
  (Attachment A) regarding responsibility for unforeseen underground conditions. Mr.
  Bennett stated that the statement can be removed.

  City Attorney Davis clarified that his office will work with staff and the contractor to develop
  an agreement to document the City Council’s intent for consideration the next meeting.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that there should also be clarification regarding the
  services provided to the HOAs.
